account: On 13 February 2026, Undark reported that there is little or no empirical evidence that AI weapons detection systems have prevented shootings in real settings such as schools. According to arrest papers cited by WCTV, Florida State University police responded to the St. Augustine parking garage at about 2:30 a.m. on Saturday 2 May 2026. ZeroEyes gun detection technology had detected an individual in black pointing a gun on the bottom level. ZeroEyes layers over existing cameras and routes human-verified detections to police. Camera footage showed Tyler Farmer, 19, brandishing a loaded firearm at four other people. Officers found a Glock 19 handgun, stolen from Miller County, Georgia, in his waistband. He was charged with possessing a firearm on school property, unlawful carry, improper display of a firearm and grand theft of a firearm. He bonded out on Sunday 3 May 2026. The Tallahassee Democrat, citing court records, says that police responded to a “ZeroEyes camera notification” and that Farmer is not a student at the university. FOX49 reported on 5 May 2026 that the police report credits the ZeroEyes notification with helping officers respond more quickly and know what they faced. The university declined to say when it bought the system or why.

Human analysts verify detections before alerts, so the AI's contribution is the initial detection. Both sources are local news citing arrest papers. Neither quantifies response time or states whether anyone else had called police.
